Philosophy

How I approach my work.

I start with the problem, build the smallest useful version, and remove anything that makes the product harder to understand or maintain.

  • 01

    Simplicity

    I keep interfaces and code focused on the task at hand.

  • 02

    Purpose

    Every feature should solve a problem that a user can recognize.

  • 03

    Balance

    I consider maintainability, performance, accessibility, and visual design together.

  • 04

    Continuous Improvement

    I use each release to learn what should be kept, changed, or removed.

In practice, KISS and YAGNI keep the scope small. DRY is useful when shared code reduces maintenance; unnecessary abstraction makes code harder to read. SOLID and GRASP help separate responsibilities so later changes remain manageable.

About

About Japandi Dev

Japandi Dev is my anonymous space for sharing software projects and experiments.

The name comes from Japandi design: Japanese restraint combined with Scandinavian warmth and function.

I use the same idea in software by favoring clear structure, useful features, and fewer distractions.
